 LA JOLLA, Calif. –  UC San Diego looks to get back on track as the Tritons (2-1) welcome Texas Southern to LionTree Arena on Military Appreciation Night. Last time out, the Tritons lost at Utah State. Meantime, the Tigers (1-3) are in search of their first road victory of the season.
The Tritons and Tigers will be meeting for the first time when they square off at LionTree Arena Monday. Tickets can be purchased through Triton Box Office . The game can be seen on ESPN+ with Steve Quis and John Kentera. The action also airs live on 97.3 The Fan in San Diego, the free Audacy app, or SiriusXM channel 185 with Ted Mendenhall providing the play-by-play. Radio pregame coverage gets underway at 6:32 p.m. PT with Sam Levitt live courtside in La Jolla.

 WHAT'S NEXT 
UC San Diego heads to Palm Desert next weekend to take part in the Acrisure Series. The Tritons will first square off against future WCC foe Seattle U on Sunday night at 6:30 p.m. Fans can purchase a game pass to watch the action on FloSports or listen live on 97.3 The Fan in San Diego and SiriusXM channel 185. UC San Diego will play again on Monday, facing either Loyola Chicago or San José State.
 LAST TIME OUT: TRITONS 82, UTAH STATE 120 Stats 
Utah State guard Mason Falslev scored 33 points and pulled down 12 rebounds, and the Aggies hit 21 three-pointers in a 120-82 victory over visiting UC San Diego Friday night at Dee Glen Smith Spectrum. Utah State (4-0) delighted the home crowd of 9,518, shooting 62% in the win. Six Aggies finished in double figures and nine made a three-pointer.
 Treysen Eaglestaff scored 16 and Leo Beath poured in 15 for UC San Diego (2-1).
 BEATH BREAKS 1,000 
UC San Diego senior Leo Beath scored his 1,000th career point as part of a 15-point effort at Utah State (Nov. 13). Beath is one of two active Tritons with 1,000 career points, joining Treysen Eaglestaff .

 SECOND HALF STRENGTH 
Through three games, the Tritons are outscoring their opposition by 50 points in the second half. UC San Diego has trailed in all contests at halftime.
 IMPRESSIVE DEBUTS 
First-year Triton guards Rahmir Barno and Kayde Dotson had strong debuts in an opening night win over Whittier (Nov. 2). Barno scored 19 points with six rebounds, four assists, two steals and no turnovers. Dotson added a game-high 21 points (19 in the second half), sinking four three-pointers and pulling down four rebounds. Dotson's seven made field goals matched a career high.
 CONTROLLING THE GLASS 
UC San Diego outrebounded the Poets, 49-37, in the opening night victory (Nov. 2).
 FIRST-TIME STARTERS 
In the Tritons' season debut vs. Whittier (Nov. 2), Rahmir Barno , Dimitrije Vukicevic and Treysen Eaglestaff all made their first starts for UC San Diego.
 OPENING STRONG 
With the win over the Poets (Nov. 2), UC San Diego improved to 5-2 all-time in season openers as a Division I program.
 TREYSEN TAKES CHARGE 
Playing in his first game as a Triton, fifth year guard Treysen Eaglestaff stuffed the stat sheet for UC San Diego. Eaglestaff scored a game-high 29 points, sinking five three-pointers in an exhibition against USC (Oct. 17). Eaglestaff added seven rebounds, two assists, two blocks and a steal over 29 minutes.
 2025-26 REWIND 
In his first season at the helm, head coach Clint Allard '08 led the Tritons to a 23-11 record. The 23 victories are the second-most by the Tritons in the program's Division I era.
 FINAL BIG WEST POLL 
UC San Diego was selected to finish second in The Big West preseason men's basketball coaches' poll. In addition, Triton senior Leo Beath was named to the preseason coaches' team. The preseason poll and preseason team are voted on by the league's 12 head coaches.
 NO PLACE LIKE HOME 
UC San Diego has excelled inside LionTree Arena, posting a 39-9 record in La Jolla over the past three-plus seasons.
 BLUE (AND GOLD) RIBBON 
A pair of UC San Diego men's basketball scholar-athletes have been highlighted in this year's Blue Ribbon College Basketball Yearbook. Senior Leo Beath has been named to the Preseason All-Big West Team and first year Triton Rahmir Barno (Florida Gulf Coast) was selected as the conference's Newcomer of the Year by the annual publication.
 Leo Beath is in his second season in La Jolla following a breakout campaign in 2025-26. Beath was named Honorable Mention All-Big West by the league's head coaches and was crowned Tournament MVP of the Adventure Bracket at the Terry's Chocolate ESPN Events Invitational after averaging 23.6 points in three UC San Diego victories, leading the Tritons to the championship title. Last season, Beath was UC San Diego's leading scorer at 12.2 points per game. Other accolades from a season ago include being selected by the USBWA as Oscar Robertson National Player of the Week and Lou Henson National Player of the Week in December.
A Philadelphia native, Rahmir Barno joined UC San Diego after spending three seasons at Florida Gulf Coast University. He registered the second most assists and assists per game in the ASUN conference as a junior, ranking 38th nationally. Barno notched three point-assist double-doubles, averaging 11.5 points and 31.5 minutes per game.
 BIG FINALE ON THE WEST COAST 
UC San Diego is in its final season competing in The Big West. The men's basketball program – and most Triton teams – will transition to the West Coast Conference in July.
 About UC San Diego Athletics 
 After two decades as one of the most successful programs in NCAA Division II, the UC San Diego intercollegiate athletics program has begun a new era as a member of The Big West in NCAA Division I. The 24-sport Tritons earned 30 team and nearly 150 individual national championships during its time in Divisions II and III and helped guide 1,400 scholar-athletes to All-America honors. A total of 84 Tritons have earned Academic All-America honors, while 39 have garnered prestigious NCAA Post Graduate Scholarships. UC San Diego scholar-athletes exemplify the academic ideals of one of the world's preeminent institutions, graduating at an average rate of 90 percent, the highest rate among public institutions in NCAA Division I or II. For more information on the Tritons, visit UCSDtritons.com or follow UC San Diego Athletics on social media @UCSDtritons.
